column1: # Verilog-AMS real-net corpus: cases RSpice is checked against a reference
# model rather than against another simulator.
#   <corpus-relative .v path>\t<note>
# There is no oracle column here, and that is the difference from
# `../verilog-manifest.tsv` rather than an omission.
# The sibling corpus is IEEE 1364-2005 Verilog, and its cases are compared
# against Icarus Verilog and Verilator — two simulators written by other people
# that both implement that standard. These cases are Verilog-AMS LRM 2.4
# section 3.7's `wreal`, which is a different standard, and neither oracle
# implements it in a form this harness could hold to an answer. Pointing them
# at a case they cannot run would produce a compile failure the harness would
# have to learn to ignore, and an ignored failure is how an oracle arm stops
# meaning anything.
# So these cases live in their own directory with their own manifest, and the
# Icarus and Verilator arms never see them: `discover_designs` in
# `crates/rspice-conformance/src/suites/verilog/corpus.rs` reads files rather
# than recursing, so a subdirectory is invisible to the corpus beside it. The
# same reason `scale/` is a subdirectory.
# What replaces the oracle is a reference model: for each case, an independent
# computation of the expected trace in `crates/rspice-conformance/tests/
# verilog_ams.rs`, written from the clause rather than read off a run. That is
# a weaker guarantee than two foreign simulators agreeing and it is stated as
# one — but it is not weaker than nothing, because the model and the design are
# written in different languages against the same paragraph, and the arithmetic
# that produced each number is beside it.
# `wrealsum`, `wrealavg`, `wrealmin` and `wrealmax` are not Accellera's. See
# `wreal_resolution.v` and `WrealResolution` for what they are and why RSpice
# implements them under those names.
wreal_forms.v
column2: real nets end to end: a real port, real arithmetic, a DAC ladder driven by four-state conditions, a comparison to bits, and the section 3.7 value-change event

column1: wreal_resolution.v
column2: the four resolved real-net spellings on identical driver pairs, and an undriven wreal reading zero per section 3.7

column1: real_state.v
column2: real state across a clock edge: a module-level `real` filter written with `<=`, a process-local `real` accumulating across a suspension, a `parameter real` folded into the recurrence, an `output real` variable port, and the section 3.7 `$realtobits`/`$bitstoreal` round trip
